### Server uptime

**`serverStatus.uptime`** — seconds the current **mongod** process has been running.

**Unit:** seconds (displayed as duration)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.uptime`

---

### How to read

- Monotonic increase while the process is up
- **Drop** or reset → **restart** (mark the timestamp)
- May not start at zero if the dashboard time range begins mid-run

---

### Troubleshooting

- Restart + memory drop → OOM · **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)**, **Swap Memory**
- Restart + assert spike → crash · **Asserts**
- Planned maintenance → correlate with deploy window
- After restart, counters reset · **Operations**, **Page Faults** rates may look odd briefly

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)

### Asserts

Per-second rate of **`serverStatus.asserts`** — mongod internal checks and user-triggered assertion counters.

**Unit:** asserts/sec (`ops`)

**Expectation:** normally **flat at zero**; any sustained non-zero rate warrants investigation.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`serverStatus.asserts.regular`
`serverStatus.asserts.warning`
`serverStatus.asserts.msg`
`serverStatus.asserts.user`
`serverStatus.asserts.rollovers`

**Query type:** cumulative counter → `derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` → `aggregateWindow(mean)`

**Rollovers:** count of times assert counters wrapped past 2³⁰ — spikes are rare and distinct from error asserts.

---

### How to read

- **Regular** / **Msg** — internal mongod assertion failures (unusual)
- **Warning** — non-fatal internal warnings
- **User** — client-visible errors (duplicate key, validation, disk full, etc.)
- **Rollovers** — counter wrap events, not application errors
- Brief spikes on restart or deploy may appear as counter resets

---

### Troubleshooting

- **Regular** or **Msg** sustained → possible bug or corruption · check mongod logs immediately
- **User** spikes → application errors · correlate with app logs and **Operations**
- Spike + **Server uptime** drop → crash/assert abort · **Replica Members Health**
- Zero across all lines → healthy (typical)

Correlate with **Server uptime** and **Average Operation Latency**.

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — asserts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.asserts)

### WiredTiger ticket availability

Shows how many **read** and **write** execution tickets are still available in the storage engine. Each ticket allows one concurrent operation; when **available** reaches **0**, new operations wait until a ticket is freed.

**Unit:** ticket count (not bytes)

---

### Metrics (same concept, two paths)

**MongoDB 8.x+**  
`serverStatus.queues.execution.read.available`  
`serverStatus.queues.execution.write.available`

**Legacy**  
`serverStatus.wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions.read.available`  
`serverStatus.wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions.write.available`

Both paths queried for compatibility. Usually only one has data per version.

---

### How to read

- Two lines: read and write **available** tickets  
- **stepAfter** reflects discrete ticket changes  
- Typical max ~**128** (dynamic adjustment on 7.0+)

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained **low or zero** → concurrency saturation  
- Correlate with **Current Queue writers / readers** and **Average Operation Latency**

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [Performance tuning — WiredTiger tickets](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/performance-tuning/)

### WiredTiger cache size

**maximum bytes configured** vs **bytes currently in the cache** — WiredTiger internal cache limit and current usage. **Unit:** bytes (per MongoDB docs). Current usage should not exceed the configured maximum.

**Metrics:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.maximum bytes configured` · `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.bytes currently in the cache`

To change the limit, see `wiredTigerCacheSizeGB` / `storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB` (config in GB; these stats are still bytes).

---

### How to read

- Two lines: configured max and current usage
- WiredTiger often targets ~80% of max under load; sustained saturation → eviction pressure

---

### Troubleshooting

- Usage near max → **Pages Evicted**, **Dirty Cache Bytes**
- Consistently at max → raise `cacheSizeGB` or reduce working set

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

### WiredTiger Pages Evicted

Rate of **modified** (dirty) and **unmodified** (clean) cache pages evicted per second. MongoDB docs note unmodified evictions as the main eviction statistic.

**Unit:** pages/s (derivative of cumulative counters)

---

**Fields:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.modified pages evicted` · `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.unmodified pages evicted`

- **Modified pages evicted (dirty)** — evicted after write/reconciliation
- **Unmodified pages evicted (clean)** — discarded without write

---

### Troubleshooting

- Dirty eviction spikes → cache pressure, write latency · **WiredTiger Cache**, **Dirty Cache Bytes**
- Eviction can't keep up → app threads may evict (performance cliff)

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

- Resident near system RAM → swap risk · **Swap Memory**, **Page Faults**

- High rate + high **Network In / Out** bytesOut → large responses · check projections/limits

### Page faults

Rate of `extra_info.page_faults` (cumulative counter since process start). Page faults occur when MongoDB must access data not in physical memory. Per MongoDB docs, limited sporadic faults are normal; sustained high rates often mean the working set exceeds RAM.

**Unit:** page faults/sec (Grafana `ops`)

**Note:** On Windows, hard and soft page faults are both counted; fields in `extra_info` vary by platform.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.extra_info.page_faults`

---

### How to read

- Single line · spikes → memory pressure or cold data access
- Flat near zero → working set mostly in memory

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained high rate → working set > RAM · correlate with **WiredTiger Cache**, **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)**, **Swap Memory**
- Spikes during scans/index builds → expected · check query patterns if persistent
- High faults + active swap → add RAM or reduce working set

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — extra_info](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#extra_info)

### Average operation latency

Rolling average latency per operation type, derived from cumulative `opLatencies` counters.

**Formula:** `derivative(*.latency) / derivative(*.ops)` → **µs per operation** (same as Δlatency / Δops over each window).

**Unit:** microseconds (`µs`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.opLatencies.reads.latency` · `serverStatus.opLatencies.reads.ops`
- `serverStatus.opLatencies.writes.latency` · `serverStatus.opLatencies.writes.ops`
- `serverStatus.opLatencies.commands.latency` · `serverStatus.opLatencies.commands.ops`

---

### How to read

- Three lines: read, write, command average latency
- Spikes → slower operations in that class
- Flat at **0** → no ops in window (idle), not zero latency

---

### Troubleshooting

- Spikes + low **WiredTiger Tickets** → concurrency contention
- Spikes + disk I/O → storage bottleneck · **Page Faults**, **Disk I/O**
- Latency up, ops down → **Operations Latencies Op**, **Operations**
- Commands line often highest → includes admin/aggregate work

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — opLatencies](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.opLatencies)

### Cursors

**Open cursors** from **`metrics.cursor.open.*`** (current count, gauge). **`metrics.cursor.timedOut`** is a **cumulative counter** — shown here as **timeouts per second** (derivative).

**Unit:** count (`short`) for open · timeouts/sec (`ops`) for timed out rate

---

### Metrics

**Fields (open — gauge, `last`):**

- `serverStatus.metrics.cursor.open.total`
- `serverStatus.metrics.cursor.open.noTimeout`
- `serverStatus.metrics.cursor.open.pinned`

**Field (timeouts — counter, `derivative(1s)`):**

- `serverStatus.metrics.cursor.timedOut`

---

### How to read

- **Open total** — cursors mongod holds for clients; usually small
- **Open (no timeout)** / **Open (pinned)** — subsets of total
- **Timed out (/sec)** — idle cursors killed (default cursor timeout ~10 min)
- **stepAfter** on open lines reflects discrete count changes

---

### Troubleshooting

- **Open total** rising → possible cursor leak (app not closing/exhausting cursors)
- **Timed out (/sec)** rising → clients abandoning cursors · correlate with **Operations** (getmore/query)
- Tailable / pinned cursors can keep **open** elevated without a leak

---

### Admin Commands (metrics.commands)

Per-second rate of selected **`serverStatus.metrics.commands.*.total`** counters — admin/catalog-style commands tracked individually by MongoDB.

**Not** the same as **Operations** (`opcounters.command`), which rolls up non-opcounter command traffic (**including aggregate**); this panel tracks specific `metrics.commands.*` counters individually.

**Unit:** commands per second (`ops`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.metrics.commands.createIndexes.total`
- `serverStatus.metrics.commands.dataSize.total`
- `serverStatus.metrics.commands.dropIndexes.total`
- `serverStatus.metrics.commands.listCollections.total`
- `serverStatus.metrics.commands.listDatabases.total`
- `serverStatus.metrics.commands.listIndexes.total`

- One line per command counter above

- Sustained high list* rates → chatty clients or health checks · compare with **Network Requests**

- For overall op mix, use **Operations**; for document volume, **Documents**

---

### Replica members lag

Wall-clock replication lag per member:

**Formula:** `(serverStatus.localTime − members.N.lastAppliedWallTime) / 1000` → **seconds**

Both timestamps are **milliseconds** in FTDC; the query converts the delta to seconds.

**Unit:** seconds (`s`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.localTime`
- `replSetGetStatus.members.0.lastAppliedWallTime` … `replSetGetStatus.members.4.lastAppliedWallTime`

Member **N** is the array index in `replSetGetStatus.members` (not necessarily hostname order).

---

### How to read

- One line per member index (0–4)
- **~0** → caught up (primary or healthy secondary)
- Rising trend on a secondary → replication falling behind
- **Gap** (not 0) for missing member slots — no `lastAppliedWallTime` in FTDC for that index

---

### Troubleshooting

- Secondary lag rising → disk I/O, CPU, network on that node · **Opcounters Replica**, **Disk I/O**
- Lag spikes during checkpoints → I/O contention
- Primary throttling → **FlowControl isLagged** · **Replica Members Ping**
- Member down → **Replica Members Health**

---

### Docs

- [replSetGetStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetGetStatus/)
- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)

**`replSetGetStatus.members.N.pingMs`** — round-trip time in **milliseconds** from **this FTDC host** to each replica set member (repl heartbeat).

**Unit:** milliseconds (`ms`)

**Note:** **N** is the member array index in `replSetGetStatus.members`, not hostname order. Use the **hostname** template variable to pick which mongod’s view of the set you are viewing.

### Oplog storage size

Disk space allocated to the **`local.oplog.rs`** capped collection (`collStats` / `storageStats`). **Oplog storage size** is total allocation on disk; **Oplog free storage** is unused space within that allocation.

**Unit:** bytes (`bytes`)

**Not `dbStats.storageSize`:** FTDC exposes oplog **collStats** here, not per-database storage totals.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`local.oplog.rs.stats.storageStats.storageSize`
`local.oplog.rs.stats.storageStats.freeStorageSize`

Snapshot gauge — **`aggregateWindow(..., fn: last)`**, no derivative.

---

### How to read

- **Oplog storage size** — grows as the capped oplog fills its on-disk allocation (does not shrink when entries roll off)
- **Oplog free storage** — headroom within that allocation
- **Used ≈ storage size − free storage** at each point
- Flat **storage size** with falling **free storage** → oplog nearing capacity

---

### Troubleshooting

- Step change + write workload shift → larger oplog entries · more replication network/disk

- **Arbiter / standalone** may show no or stale series (no meaningful oplog)

### Current queue (writers / readers)

**Unit:** count (`short`)

**Note:** On MongoDB 4.2+, these queues are often **0**; use **WiredTiger Tickets** and **Average Operation Latency** for concurrency pressure on modern releases.

- Two lines: queued readers vs writers

- Persistent read queue → long-running reads blocking others
- Always zero but slow DB → focus on tickets/latency, not this panel alone

---

### Docs

### Query executor

Per-second rates from **queryExecutor** counters — how much work the query engine does examining indexes and documents.

**Unit:** operations/sec (`ops`) — keys scanned, docs scanned, and collection-scan events are all counter derivatives.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor.scanned` — index keys examined (`totalKeysExamined` in explain())
- `serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor.scannedObjects` — documents examined (`totalDocsExamined`)
- `serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor.collectionScans.total` — queries that performed a **collection scan** (COLLSCAN)

All are cumulative counters; query uses **`derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)`**.

---

### How to read

- **Index keys scanned / sec** — index traversal volume
- **Documents scanned / sec** — document examination volume (often dominates I/O)
- **Collection scans / sec** (right axis) — queries **not** using a useful index; should stay near **0** in production

**Keys vs docs:** high docs with low keys can mean wide index scans or many docs per key; high docs with high **Collection scans** confirms COLLSCAN.

Compare with **Query Targeting: Scanned Objects / Returned** (ratio) and **Documents** (`document.returned`).

---

### Troubleshooting

- High **Documents scanned** + high targeting ratio → missing/poor indexes · run `explain()` on slow queries
- Sustained **Collection scans / sec** → enable profiler / Performance Advisor · fix query patterns or add indexes
- High scan rates + **Page Faults** / **Disk I/O** → storage pressure from inefficient reads
- **Operations** `opcounters.query` rising with scan rates → read-heavy workload under index stress

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — metrics.queryExecutor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.metrics.queryExecutor)

### Operations (opcounters)

Per-second rate of **`serverStatus.opcounters`** — **operation-level** counts (one bulk/multi-doc op = one op). Not the same as **Documents** (`metrics.document`), which counts documents touched.

**Unit:** operations per second (`ops`)

**Note:** `opcounters.command` counts commands **not** already tracked as insert, update, delete, query, or getmore — **including aggregate** and other admin/catalog commands.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.opcounters.command`
- `serverStatus.opcounters.delete`
- `serverStatus.opcounters.getmore`
- `serverStatus.opcounters.insert`
- `serverStatus.opcounters.query`
- `serverStatus.opcounters.update`

**Query:** `derivative(..., unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` → ops/sec

---

### How to read

- Six lines: command, delete, getmore, insert, query, update **rates**
- Sudden drop → blocking or idle period
- Spike → load burst; check **Average Operation Latency** and **WiredTiger Tickets**

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained high write ops + latency → **Current Queue writers / readers**, disk I/O
- High **query** + **getmore** → cursor-heavy workload
- On secondaries, use **Opcounters Replica** instead of this panel

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — opcounters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.opcounters)

panels.description:
### Replication opcounters (If secondary)

Per-second rates from **`serverStatus.opcountersRepl`** — operations applied when this member is acting as a **secondary** (oplog apply).

**Unit:** operations/sec (`ops`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.opcountersRepl.insert`
- `serverStatus.opcountersRepl.query`
- `serverStatus.opcountersRepl.update`
- `serverStatus.opcountersRepl.delete`
- `serverStatus.opcountersRepl.getmore`
- `serverStatus.opcountersRepl.command`

Cumulative counters; query uses **`derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)`**.

---

### How to read

- Six lines · replication apply rate by type
- **View a secondary hostname** — answers “how fast is this node applying replication?”
- **Primary / write source** — expect near-zero or unhelpful lines; switch host or open **Operations (write source)**
- Fractional ops/sec → normal with sparse FTDC sampling
- **0** → idle or no replication apply in window

Compare with **Operations (write source)** on the primary, **Replica Members Lag**, **Flow control is lagged**.

---

### Troubleshooting

- Repl rates drop + **lag rising** → secondary cannot keep up · disk I/O, CPU, **Disk I/O**
- Primary **Operations (write source)** high, secondary repl low → bottleneck on secondary
- Repl **update** ≫ primary **update** → expected replication amplification
- **Flow control is lagged** = 1 + lag → primary throttling writes

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — opcountersRepl](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.opcountersRepl)

### Operation latency ops

Per-second rates from **opLatencies.*.ops** counters — how many read, write, and command operations ran in each latency class.

**Unit:** operations/sec (`ops`)

This is the **denominator** for **Average Operation Latency** (`derivative(latency) / derivative(ops)` → µs/op).

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.opLatencies.reads.ops`
- `serverStatus.opLatencies.writes.ops`
- `serverStatus.opLatencies.commands.ops`

Cumulative counters; query uses **`derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)`**.

**Not the same as opcounters:** `opLatencies` groups reads / writes / commands for latency stats; **Operations** uses `opcounters.*` (query, insert, update, delete, getmore, command).

---

### How to read

- **Read / write / command ops / sec** — throughput per latency class
- **Commands** often includes admin, aggregate, and other command work
- Fractional values → normal with sparse FTDC sampling
- **0** → idle window for that class

Compare with **Average Operation Latency** (numerator/denominator) and **Operations** (opcounters workload mix).

---

### Troubleshooting

- **Ops up, avg latency up** → load + slower per-op work
- **Ops down, avg latency up** → fewer ops but each slower (contention, I/O)
- **Ops up, avg latency flat** → healthy scale-out of throughput
- Read/write imbalance → workload skew · correlate with **Query Executor**, **Documents**, **Disk I/O**

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — opLatencies](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.opLatencies)

panels.description:
### Query targeting: scanned objects / returned

Ratio of **document scan rate** to **document return rate**:

**Formula:** `derivative(scannedObjects, 1s) / derivative(document.returned, 1s)`

Same idea as **totalDocsExamined / docs returned** in explain() — aggregated over time.

**Unit:** dimensionless ratio (`none`) — **1.0** ≈ one doc examined per doc returned

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor.scannedObjects`
- `serverStatus.metrics.document.returned`

Both are cumulative counters; query uses **`derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)`** before the ratio.

---

### How to read

- Single line · **Scanned / returned ratio**
- **~1** → strong targeting (most examined docs were returned)
- **> 1** (especially **10+**) → scans dominate · missing/poor indexes or large in-memory filters
- **Gap** (not 0) → no returned docs in window or zero denominator — **not** “perfect”

---

### Troubleshooting

- High ratio + high **Documents returned** → **Query Executor** · run `explain()` on hot queries
- Correlate with **Page Faults**, **Disk I/O**, **Average Operation Latency**
- **Collection scans** on **Query Executor** (right axis) confirms full collection scans

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — metrics.queryExecutor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.metrics.queryExecutor)
- [serverStatus — metrics.document](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.metrics.document)

  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["version"] =~ /^${version:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) =>
      r["_field"] == "serverStatus.metrics.document.returned" or
      r["_field"] == "serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor.scannedObjects")
  |> drop(columns: ["hostname", "version"])
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)

panels.description:
### CPU usage

Host CPU time by mode, from FTDC **systemMetrics** (OS counters in milliseconds). Each line is that mode’s share of total CPU time in the window after per-mode `derivative(1s)`.

**Formula:** `aggregateWindow(last)` → `pivot` → `derivative(*_ms, 1s)` → `(mode_ms / total_ms) × 100`

**Unit:** percent (`percent`, 0–100)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms`
`systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms`
`systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms`
`systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms`
`systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms`
`systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms`
`systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms`

**Plotted:** user, system, iowait percentages only. Idle, nice, softirq, and steal are included in **total_ms** (denominator) but not shown as separate lines.

**Query type:** computed ratio (not a single counter derivative). Output uses `_field` / `_value` via `union` for Grafana.

---

### How to read

- **User %** — application time (mongod, queries, aggregations)
- **System (kernel) %** — kernel time, syscalls, context switching
- **I/O wait %** — CPU idle while waiting on disk
- Three lines sum to **≤ 100%** (unplotted modes account for the rest)

---

### Troubleshooting

- High **User %** with **Operations** or **Query Executor** → CPU-bound workload
- High **I/O wait %** → disk bottleneck · **Disk I/O**, **WiredTiger Block Manager**, **Page Faults**
- High **System %** with many **Connections** → thread/syscall overhead
- VM steal not plotted — inspect raw `systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms` in Explore if host may be oversubscribed

Correlate with **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)** and **System Memory**.

---

### Docs

- FTDC **systemMetrics** (OS-level; not `serverStatus`)

base =
  from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "ftdc")
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r["hostname"] =~ /^${hostname:regex}$/)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r["version"] =~ /^${version:regex}$/)
    |> filter(fn: (r) =>
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms" or
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms" or
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms" or
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms" or
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms" or
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms" or
        r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms")
    |> drop(columns: ["hostname", "version"])
    |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
    |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
    |> derivative(
        unit: 1s,
        nonNegative: true,
        columns: [
          "systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms",
          "systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms",
          "systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms",
          "systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms",
          "systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms",
          "systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms",
          "systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms",
        ],
      )
    |> map(fn: (r) => ({
        _time: r._time,
        user_ms: float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms"]),
        system_ms: float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms"]),
        iowait_ms: float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms"]),
        total_ms:
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms"]) +
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms"]) +
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms"]) +
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms"]) +
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms"]) +
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms"]) +
          float(v: r["systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms"]),
      }))

union(tables: [
  base |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      _field: "User %",
      _value: if r.total_ms > 0.0 then 100.0 * r.user_ms / r.total_ms else 0.0,
    })),
  base |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      _field: "System (kernel) %",
      _value: if r.total_ms > 0.0 then 100.0 * r.system_ms / r.total_ms else 0.0,
    })),
  base |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      _field: "I/O wait %",
      _value: if r.total_ms > 0.0 then 100.0 * r.iowait_ms / r.total_ms else 0.0,
    })),
])
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)

panels.description:
### System memory

Host RAM from FTDC **systemMetrics** (`/proc/meminfo`, values stored as **kB**). Shows how much memory the OS reports as **available** vs **free**.

**Unit:** bytes (Grafana auto-scale; FTDC fields are `*_kb`, query multiplies by 1024)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`systemMetrics.memory.MemAvailable_kb`
`systemMetrics.memory.MemFree_kb`

**MemAvailable** — estimate of memory startable for new workloads without swapping (includes reclaimable cache).

**MemFree** — completely unallocated pages (often much lower than available).

---

### How to read

- **Memory available** — primary signal for OS headroom
- **Memory free** — strictly idle RAM; low free + healthy available is normal on Linux
- Both lines fall when mongod, page cache, or other services consume RAM

---

### Troubleshooting

- **Available** trending toward zero → memory pressure · **Swap Memory**, **Page Faults**, **WiredTiger Cache**
- Available low but **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)** moderate → other processes or OS page cache
- Available and free both low + high **CPU Usage** I/O wait → possible thrashing
- After mongod restart, available may jump as RSS is released

Correlate with **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)** and **Swap Memory**.

---

### Docs

- FTDC **systemMetrics** (OS-level; not `serverStatus`)
- Linux [meminfo](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/mm/memory-model.html) — `MemAvailable` vs `MemFree`

panels.title: System Memory

panels.description:
### Swap memory

Host swap from FTDC **systemMetrics** (`/proc/meminfo`, values stored as **kB**). Shows **used**, **free**, and **total** swap capacity. **Swap used** is computed as `SwapTotal − SwapFree`.

**Unit:** bytes (Grafana auto-scale; FTDC fields are `*_kb`, query multiplies by 1024)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`systemMetrics.memory.SwapTotal_kb`
`systemMetrics.memory.SwapFree_kb`

**Computed:** Swap used = `SwapTotal_kb − SwapFree_kb` (not a separate FTDC field)

**Plotted:** Swap used (computed) · Swap free · Swap total

---

### How to read

- **Swap used** — should stay at **0** on a MongoDB host
- **Swap free** — unused swap capacity
- **Swap total** — configured swap size (may be **0** if swap is disabled)
- **Swap used + Swap free ≈ Swap total** at each point

---

### Troubleshooting

**Formula:** `derivative(io_queued_ms, 1s)` → **ms/s** (milliseconds of queue wait accrued per wall-clock second)

**Unit:** ms/s — **not** in-flight I/O count · **not** `read_time_ms` / `write_time_ms` (**Disk I/O Busy Time**)

**Not mongod-only:** OS view of all processes on the host.

**Saturation hint:** sustained values toward **~1000 ms/s** → persistent queueing on that device.

- Sustained high ms/s → disk saturation · **Disk I/O Busy Time**, **Disk I/O**, **CPU Usage** I/O wait

### Network In / Out

Per-second **logical** network throughput for **mongod** — cumulative **`serverStatus.network.bytesIn`** / **`bytesOut`**.

**Unit:** B/s (`Bps`) — `derivative(unit: 1s)` on byte counters

**Logical bytes:** BSON/document size as counted by mongod (not necessarily on-wire size). Compare with **Network Physical In / Out** for compression/wire bytes.

`serverStatus.network.bytesIn`

**Query type:** cumulative counter → `derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` → `aggregateWindow(mean)`

- **Logical bytes in** — data received by mongod
- **Logical bytes out** — data sent to clients / other nodes
- Secondary: often **in ≥ out** during replication catch-up
- Primary: **out** rises with large query results or replication fan-out

### Troubleshooting

- High **bytes out** + high **Documents** returned → large result sets · check projections/`limit`
- High bytes + low **Operations** → big payloads per op
- Logical ≫ physical on **Network Physical In / Out** → compression effective (normal)
- Logical ≈ physical → little compression · replication or already-compressed payloads
- Bytes flat but lag → **Replica Members Lag**, **TCP InSegs / OutSegs**, **Replica Members Ping**

Correlate with **Network requests** and **Operations**.

---

- [serverStatus — network](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.network)

### Network In / Out Physical

Per-second **physical (on-the-wire)** network throughput for **mongod** — cumulative **`serverStatus.network.physicalBytesIn`** / **`physicalBytesOut`**.

**Unit:** B/s (`Bps`) — `derivative(unit: 1s)` on byte counters

**Physical vs logical:** **Physical** = bytes sent/received on network connections (wire size, after compression where applicable). **Logical** = document/BSON bytes as counted by mongod · compare **Network In / Out**.

**Not disk I/O:** network bytes, not storage · see **Disk I/O** for block device throughput.

### How to read

- **Physical bytes in** — wire bytes received by mongod

- **Logical > physical** on paired panels → compression saving bandwidth (common on replication)
- **Logical ≈ physical** → little compression benefit on the wire

---

- High physical **out** on primary → replication + client traffic · **Replica Members Lag**, **TCP InSegs / OutSegs**
- High physical **in** on secondary → replication catch-up
- Physical throughput near link capacity → timeouts, lag · **Replica Members Ping**
- High physical + low **Operations** → large compressed payloads or oplog batches

Correlate with **Network In / Out** (logical) and **Network requests**.

### TCP connection lifecycle

Per-second rates of host **TCP connection lifecycle counters** from FTDC **systemMetrics** (`/proc/net/snmp`).

**Unit:** events/sec — `derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` on cumulative counters

**Not mongod-only:** whole-host TCP stack.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:ActiveOpens`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:AttemptFails`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:EstabResets`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:OutRsts`

**Query type:** cumulative counter → `derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` → `aggregateWindow(mean)`

**Not this panel:** `Tcp:CurrEstab` (open connection **count**, gauge — use `last`, not derivative)

---

### How to read

- **TCP active opens** — successful new connections initiated (normally **> 0** on a busy host)
- **TCP connect failures** — failed connection attempts (expect **~0**)
- **TCP established resets** — established connections reset (expect **~0**)
- **TCP RST sent** — segments with RST flag (expect **~0**)
- Brief spikes during deploys/restarts are normal

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained **AttemptFails** → refused connections · firewall, `ulimit`, mongod down, wrong port
- **EstabResets** / **RST sent** → mid-connection drops · **Replica Members Health**, node restarts
- High **ActiveOpens** with errors → churny clients or replication mesh · compare **TCP InSegs / OutSegs**
- With **TCP Packet Loss or Corruption** → loss before reset
- With lag → **Replica Members Lag**, **Replica Members Ping**

Correlate with **TCP InSegs / OutSegs** and **Replica Members Health**.

---

### Docs

- FTDC **systemMetrics** (OS-level; not `serverStatus`)
- Linux [SNMP-TCP-MIB / netstat](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/networking/snmp_counter.html)

### TCP routing issues

Per-second rates of host **IP routing and fragmentation error counters** from FTDC **systemMetrics** (`/proc/net/snmp`).

**Unit:** events/sec — `derivative(unit: 1s)` on cumulative counters

**Layer note:** these are **IP** counters (title says “TCP routing” historically). **Not mongod-only.**

**Expectation:** normally **flat at zero**; any sustained rate → routing, MTU, or path problems.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`systemMetrics.netstat.Ip:OutNoRoutes`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Ip:FragFails`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Ip:ReasmFails`

**Query type:** cumulative counter → `derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` → `aggregateWindow(mean)`

**Not ingested (optional FTDC `IpExt` paths):** `IpExt:InNoRoutes` · `IpExt:InTruncatedPkts` — add to `metrics_to_get.txt` if present in your `metrics.txt`

**Not this panel:** `Ip:InDiscards` / `Ip:OutDiscards` → **TCP Packet Loss or Corruption**

---

### How to read

- **IP no route (out)** — packets dropped with no route to destination
- **IP fragmentation failures** — could not fragment (often **MTU / PMTU** issues)
- **IP reassembly failures** — fragmented packets could not be reassembled

---

### Troubleshooting

- **OutNoRoutes** → wrong/missing routes, asymmetric routing, firewall blackholes
- **FragFails** / **ReasmFails** → **MTU mismatch** (VPN, cloud network, jumbo frames)
- With **TCP Packet Loss or Corruption** → broader stack problems
- Intermittent app errors → **Replica Members Ping**, **TCP Connection Issues**

Correlate with **TCP InSegs / OutSegs** and **Replica Members Health**.

---

### Docs

- FTDC **systemMetrics** (OS-level; not `serverStatus`)
- Linux [SNMP / netstat counters](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/networking/snmp_counter.html)

### TCP packet loss or corruption

Per-second rates of host **TCP/IP error and discard counters** from FTDC **systemMetrics** (`/proc/net/snmp`).

**Unit:** events/sec — `derivative(unit: 1s)` on cumulative counters

**Not mongod-only:** whole-host TCP/IP stack (all processes).

**Expectation:** normally **flat at zero**; any sustained non-zero rate warrants investigation.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:InCsumErrors`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:InErrs`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Tcp:RetransSegs`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Ip:InDiscards`
`systemMetrics.netstat.Ip:OutDiscards`

**Query type:** cumulative counter → `derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)` → `aggregateWindow(mean)`

**Optional (in `metrics_to_get.txt`, not plotted):** `Ip:FragFails` · `Ip:ReasmFails` (fragmentation/reassembly failures)

---

### How to read

- **TCP retransmissions** — packet loss / timeout on the wire (most common “loss” signal)
- **TCP checksum errors** — corrupted frames received
- **TCP input errors** — other inbound TCP errors
- **IP discards** — kernel dropped packets (buffers, policy, congestion)

---

### Troubleshooting

- **RetransSegs** sustained → loss/congestion · **Replica Members Ping**, **Average Operation Latency**
- **InCsumErrors** → bad cable/NIC/driver, offload bugs
- **InDiscards** / **OutDiscards** → buffer pressure · NIC ring, `netdev_max_backlog`, flood traffic
- Errors + high **TCP InSegs / OutSegs** → saturated or failing path
- Errors on one member only → host/NIC/path to that node · **Replica Members Health**

Correlate with **TCP InSegs / OutSegs** and **TCP Connection Issues**.

---

### Docs

- FTDC **systemMetrics** (OS-level; not `serverStatus`)
- Linux [SNMP / netstat counters](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/networking/snmp_counter.html)
